reviews.text: One would be hard pressed to find a more culturally critical cinematic work than Poitras' risky, revealing film Citizenfour.
reviews.author: Jordan M. Smith

reviews.text: So much is revealed by those leaks that it would be easy for Poitras to have buried us in data. But she lets the film unfold as a character study, with long silences and lingering close-ups as we watch Snowden come to terms...
reviews.author: Brian D. Johnson

reviews.text: Citizenfour, I had to keep reminding myself, shows us history in the making. I had to keep telling myself what I was seeing was important because most of it is otherwise pretty dull.
reviews.author: Ren Jender

reviews.text: Watching this real-time whistleblowing is nothing short of unbelievable.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Poitras takes the facts at face value considering her source is an enemy of the state, but the revelations are no less reeling.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: What seems most remarkable in that hotel room in Hong Kong is Snowden's freedom from anxiety.
reviews.author: David Bromwich

reviews.text: Laura Poitras took on a massive project when she set out to make CitizenFour, and she succeeds in capturing and unveiling this extraordinary moment in journalism that we, on the outside, never see.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: Citizenfour creates a powerful dystopia.
reviews.author: Heather Dockray

reviews.text: The profoundly personal cost of taking action is rendered explicit in the story of Edward Snowden.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: Poitras isn't there to question his motives or the rightness of his cause, she's there to bear witness. This film is her document on why his actions matter and what it cost Snowden.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: [1984] is looking less like fiction with each passing day.
reviews.author: Giovanni Fazio

reviews.text: Yes, we should be concerned about what our government is up to, but we should also be skeptical of Citizenfour.
reviews.author: Joe Bendel

reviews.text: This is film as activism, and documentary filmmaking as dissension.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: This is a brave, bold and important film.
reviews.author: Peter Calder

reviews.text: For all the film's superficial slickness, it's a mess.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: As much as it resembles a conspiracy thriller in which data encryption is a survival tactic, Citizenfour must be considered, above all, a journalistic achievement.
reviews.author: Edmund Lee

reviews.text: The most frightening aspect of the documentary is a suggestion that this is only the dawn of what's to come.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

reviews.text: A risky and revelatory documentary weakened only by its awesome source.
reviews.author: David N. Butterworth

reviews.text: Although Snowden has been depicted by his detractors as a gutless, narcissistic traitor fleeing the law, the Edward Snowden I saw in this film is quite different. He is very intelligent and is aware of the cost of his actions to himself and others.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Bold docu explores Edward Snowden's controversial actions.
reviews.author: Brian Costello

reviews.text: Citizenfour (named after Snowden's codename of choice) is paced like the great paranoid-man political thrillers of the 1970s... Poitras makes this potentially-tedious exercise seem claustrophobic in the most enthralling way.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Director Laura Poitras presents a portrait of whistleblower Edward Snowden that is neither demon not saint, though his patriotic motives are clear in that he felt he was uncovering massive abuses of authority.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Movies don't put themselves together. Every moment, every cut, and every camera angle is an editorial choice. So is the structure of the movie, which builds its mix of fear and danger sure-footedly,
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: Did the NSA have foreknowledge that Citizenfour was going to win the Oscar? Um, probably ...
reviews.author: Kimberly Gadette

reviews.text: A compelling, real-life thriller that takes us inside the mind of a whistle blower.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Vital, urgent, and breathtaking ... It is brilliant because it captures an intimate moment of history that will reverberate through the ages; a moment that would not have been captured had not a connection been made.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Laura Poitras's Oscar-nominated documentary Citizenfour is proof that you can make an espionage thriller without car chases, bikini babes or martinis.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: There's footage from within the Ecuadorian embassy in London as Julian Assange helps with the flight that takes Snowden to Moscow, where he claims political asylum. These scenes give the film an unprecedented level of immediacy and dramatic tension.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: One of its many interesting facets is how unlike the unpredictable doco model it turns out to be while still proving utterly engrossing from start to finish.
reviews.author: Steve Newall

reviews.text: Poitras' movie works even better as a horror picture -- perfect for Halloween week.
reviews.author: Richard Corliss

reviews.text: This thoughtful film is designed with taste.
reviews.author: Bill Stamets

reviews.text: The message of the movie is as clear as Siberian ice: Whether you're a Tea Partier, an Occupier or just an ordinary Joe, you might be the next citizen who's stranded in limbo.
reviews.author: Joe Williams

reviews.text: It all sounds like prophecy now, given the way things turned out.
reviews.author: T'Cha Dunlevy

reviews.text: There haven't really been any horror films that have knocked my socks off this year, but I think I would have declared Citizenfour to be the most terrifying movie of the year either way.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Citizenfour doesn't paint Snowden as a hero, but Poitras' insightful examination of his motives and personality is gripping.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The scariest thing you'll see this Halloween is Edward Snowden swearing in disbelief at the end of Laura Poitras' gripping, disturbing documentary.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: This is terrific documentary cinema.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: Citizenfour deserves your attention.
reviews.author: Edward Johnson-Ott

reviews.text: [An] absorbing character study.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Filmmaker Laura Poitras paints a frankly terrifying picture of the loss of liberty involved in the widespread government gathering of the communication done by ordinary Joes on a daily basis.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: While the film loses some urgency in its final third, it's a thrilling, shocking snapshot of a moment in time that will live in history, a reminder of the very real threat that those in power can pose to the citizens they have sworn to protect.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Much of the film consists of footage of Snowden explaining the range and depth of American data-mining to an increasingly horrified Greenwald. If it sounds dull, it isn't.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Without too much knowledge or preconceived ideas, it would make me an easy mark for a polemic about modern privacy -- but Poitras's bracing, galvanizing new documentary about the Snowden affair isn't that at all.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Despite all its paranoia, the movie does hold out a glimmer of optimism.
reviews.author: Perry Seibert

reviews.text: ... the systematic mining of communications from people the government has no reason to suspect of terrorism is indeed a thing. And, thanks to Poitras, we are there at the moment it became impossibly naive to believe otherwise.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: There will be many more movies about Snowden. But likely none will be as well-done as "Citizenfour"
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Dry yet fascinating, and always carrying an air of hushed immediacy, Citizenfour nicely documents a revelatory piece of recent history.
reviews.author: Bill Clark

reviews.text: A hard-hitting and shocking documentary about the violation of privacy by the U.S. government's massive surveillance programs.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: What an astonishing, immeasurably important historical document this is-on top of being a lock for the Best Documentary Oscar.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: Poitras' stance is simply to present the evidence, without commentary, angle or narrative.
reviews.author: Emma Morgan

reviews.text: Citizenfour argues that when we lose our personal privacy, we also lose our liberty, because fear overcomes our freedom of speech.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: It's probably the most opaque operation ever conducted on a global stage, which is why Laura Poitras's clarity is such an asset: She simply records Edward Snowden as he drops the bomb.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: Citizenfour plays like a thriller as it chronicles a complex and vitally important chapter in our history.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: Whether you consider Snowden a traitor or hero or something in between, the movie is striking in its immediacy and access and terrifying in its implications.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Compelling, eye-opening -- and terrifying.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: This is gripping, edge-of-your-seat stuff, offering the chance to experience a defining historical moment from the front lines.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: The documentary of the year may also be its most hair-raising thriller.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: How often do you see someone change the world?
reviews.author: Jeff Baker

reviews.text: So explosive, it's one of the most riveting films you'll see this year.
reviews.author: Linda Barnard

reviews.text: Citizenfour is obviously in Snowden's corner, but as an example of pure cinema vrit, this is the finest - and most disturbing - political documentary since Alex Gibney's Oscar-winning Taxi to the Dark Side.
reviews.author: Marc Savlov

reviews.text: This isn't just a documentary -- this is history.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: Thoroughly, unashamedly partisan in its presentation of the former National Security Agency systems analyst as a force for universal good.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Whatever the meaning of "the greater good" in a post-Sept. 11 world, "Citizenfour" posits - and it's hard to argue otherwise - that the right to privacy is an essential component of it.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: Like a '70s paranoia thriller with real-world consequences.
reviews.author: Michael Nordine

reviews.text: Although some scenes just rehash the content from current news stories, Citizenfour is a vital record of the evolving spy scandal that enlightens us to the identity and integrity of its whistleblower.
reviews.author: Jordan Adler

reviews.text: "Citizenfour" needs to be seen by all concerned with this issue
reviews.author: Jean Lowerison

reviews.text: A film every single American and, indeed, every world citizen should see and contemplate.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Far from just trading in conjecture and abstraction, Citizenfour self-reflexively dramatises the dangers that Snowden wants to warn us about.
reviews.author: Nick Bradshaw

reviews.text: Documentarian Laura Poitras has crafted a first-rate Hitchcockian-type thriller telling the story of Edward Snowden.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: A John le Carre film in documentary form.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Shares more DNA with such 1970s classics as The Parallax View, The Conversation or All the President's Men, than it does with most documentaries.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: This is a complicated story, but it's efficiently laid out by Poitras in this smartly edited project.
reviews.author: David Hiltbrand

reviews.text: This isn't a one-sided movie as much as it is a movie about half of one side.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: It plays out like a real-life espionage thriller, and it's horrifying in its scope.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: If you think Snowden is a traitor, you should probably see it. If you think he's a hero, you should probably see it. If you haven't made up your mind - well, you get the idea.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Alarming in the best sense of the word.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Citizenfour moves like a master spy novel.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: A first-hand, up-close account of Snowden that allows us to meet and judge the man for ourselves.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Bold, unblinking filmmaking - no less than a living document of a global scandal straight from the whistleblower. Alarming and essential - anyone with a phone should see it.
reviews.author: Simon Crook

reviews.text: The film works, whatever your ethical stance on Snowden, because it's more procedural than polemic.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Refusing to advance the story substitutes useful inquisitiveness only with unique access.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Snowden has been called a traitor, but here he comes off as a decent man trying to do the right thing, if however awkwardly (or illegally).
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: CITIZENFOUR is a documentary, an expos, a character study, a world-girdling espionage thriller, an oblique manifesto and a model of understatement. It's also a great movie.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Enter the real life world of spy craft and believe the truth is stranger than fiction.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: Calm, yet enraging. Among the most frightening and important films of the year. It must be seen by all Americans for the sake of democracy. Every U.S. government official should undergo a mandatory mental health evaluation!
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Central absorbing act is Snowden like never before-- a human being in cinema verit close-up. . .Poitras's style . . .is intimate aesthetics . . .within the eye of the storm.
reviews.author: Nora Lee Mandel

reviews.text: It's so rare to see history documented as it's happening, and "Citizenfour" succeeds in humanizing the participants without diminishing the stakes of their endeavor.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: In the end, there isn't that much to the movie apart from what Snowden has to say. Fortunately, that proves to be enough.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: It's hard to overstate the film's achievement.
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: While I consider the phrase "reality television" an oxymoron, there's nothing wrong with a good-make that great-piece of fly-on-the-wall cinma vrit to open your eyes and leave you wondering-what if "he" had stayed quiet.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: Laura Poitras may be guilty of taking Snowden at face value, but she succeeds brilliantly in evoking a shadow villain intent on world domination. Big Brother is back, baby, and he's gone digital.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: As we watch the T-shirted Snowden, sitting on his messy hotel bed with his little laptop, set the stage for what is to come, the vast disjunction between these mundane surroundings and his imminent, world-shattering revelations is almost comical.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: What comes across in "Citizenfour" is how articulate and reasonable Snowden seems, despite the crushing pressure he faces.
reviews.author: Daniel Eagan

reviews.text: Poitras' presentation of this well-known scandal feels fresh due to its intimate and first-look nature.
reviews.author: Jennifer Chang

reviews.text: Bombshell documentary conveys a fresh sense of a veil being drawn back from our eyes to reveal a shocking new world.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: [It serves as a] chance for Poitras to reorganize her Pulitzer Prize-winning story in her own medium and cinema verit style. It mostly works.
reviews.author: Andrew Lapin

reviews.text: There are not a lot of moments in documentary cinema that equal "Citizenfour."
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: Carping about as significant a film as "Citizenfour" feels beside the point. You can wish its faults didn't exist, but it does a real service in detailing what the scary consequences of those NSA actions could be.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: Citizenfour finds its strength in both the story and the telling: The information about government spying is chilling, of course, but the movie also gives us the opportunity to get to know the elusive Snowden.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: a hell of an eye opener, even given knowledge of its events. Poitras's documentary makes us feel the danger of government invasion.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Its middle section offers one of cinema's most pleasurable offerings: smart people in rooms smartly hashing things out.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: No film has ever been historic in quite the way this one is, since it tells a story in which the filmmaker and her work play a crucial part.
reviews.author: Godfrey Cheshire

reviews.text: Whether you think Edward Snowden is a hero or a traitor, you should see the riveting documentary "Citizenfour" ...
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Despite the film's virtues, we're no closer to understanding Snowden than we were a year ago when this saga began.
reviews.author: Thomas Lee

reviews.text: It's a tense and frightening thriller that blends the brisk globe-trotting of the "Bourne" movies with the spooky, atmospheric effects of a Japanese horror film.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Edward Snowden speaks. Buy a ticket to this film... and use your credit card, so the NSA knows you care about this stuff.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: The immediacy of Poitras' film is so remarkable that, at least for the immediate future, her craft is likely to be overshadowed by her access, her storytelling overshadowed by her opportunity.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: [A] twisting corkscrew of a documentary ...
reviews.author: Joe McGovern

reviews.text: A fascinating film that's also a crucial social document.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Weitzman

reviews.text: If Citizenfour ends abruptly, that's only because the real-life story is still far from over.
reviews.author: Sherilyn Connelly

reviews.text: Poitras fashions Citizenfour into a spy thriller whose intrigues bleed into everyday life.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: Poitras has made a personal film because there is no other option for this story. Her involvement changed her life, as it did the lives of her collaborators. The result is a masterful fusion of journalism and art.
reviews.author: Daniel Walber

reviews.text: 'Citizenfour' may be one of the seminal documentaries of this era.
reviews.author: Kirk Honeycutt

reviews.text: Shows another side to Snowden and the reasons for what he did in a fairly unedited fashion and that's largely what makes it the perfect coda to Snowden's story.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Poitras shows us history as it happens, scenes of such intimate momentousness that the movie's a must-see piece of work even if, in its totality, it's underwhelming as argument or cinema.
reviews.author: Alan Scherstuhl

reviews.text: You should see this movie if you're nave enough to think you have a right to privacy. But don't buy your ticket online or with a credit card.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: Laura Poitras's Citizenfour is an electrifying countdown to an epoch-altering event, unfolding in an antiseptic all-white room.
reviews.author: Melissa Anderson

reviews.text: See it exactly because so many have so much invested in keeping this quiet.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: Citizenfour does an excellent job of balancing what we already know with behind-the-scenes discussions of how the information should be released.
reviews.author: Ben Kenigsberg

reviews.text: It's rare to see this sort of candid footage, but then transparency is Snowden's mantra.
reviews.author: Ben Travis

reviews.text: It's astonishing stuff; full of bizarre revelations and incredible details that even the most paranoid conspiracy theorist would struggle to make up.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Fingers on keyboards, monitors, real-time chatting and facial beard follicles do not make for scintillating viewing.
reviews.author: Donald J. Levit

reviews.text: John le Carr couldn't have made this stuff up.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: [VIDEO ESSAY] "Citizenfour" provides a stark cinema vrit perspective on America's biggest political scandal in the country's relatively brief history.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Foremost of the film's strengths is that it wears its intelligence lightly; it educates even as it entertains.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A sobering look at what the American government, at least, is doing in the name of security.
reviews.author: Karen Krizanovich

reviews.text: The fascination of the documentary lies in the fact that Poitras was there with her camera at the crucial moments, when Snowden was sharing the information that would cause such convulsions all over the world.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: An is an expertly crafted expose with unprecedented urgency.
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: The intimacy and immediacy of the situations and experiences it does portray are compelling and satisfying enough to stick with viewers for long after the film has ended.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: Citizenfour is at its most eye-opening and essential simply as a portrait of the then 29-year-old Snowden at a point of absolute no-return in his life.
reviews.author: Dave Calhoun

reviews.text: It's a real-life thriller which, although dense and demanding of the viewer, is never less than completely gripping.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: The film's very existence stands as testament to the fact that while we maybe cowering under the corporate jackboot, we still have the power of expression, and that's all we need to get the resistance moving.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: Citizenfour is a gripping record of how our rulers are addicted to gaining more and more power and control over us - if we let them.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Everybody needs to see it.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: While hardly a riveting spy story, this documentary reveals much of whistleblower Edward Snowden's character while warning of a dangerous loss of civil liberties in America.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: "Citizenfour" shows that Snowden, the guy with the guts to expose these shadowy practices, is the one who pays the biggest price. Senators lie and congressmen squirm, and nobody is held accountable. Nobody, that is, except Snowden.
reviews.author: Drew Taylor

reviews.text: "Citizenfour" is an urgent, gripping real-life spy story that should be seen by every American, and quite likely by everybody else too.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: Laura Poitras teaches by example, providing a privileged insight into Edward Snowden's personality and motivation while keeping the focus on government spying.
reviews.author: Elise Nakhnikian

reviews.text: Quite possibly the strongest documentary about secret state intervention in private lives ...
reviews.author: Howard Feinstein

reviews.text: No matter one's personal stance about what Snowden did, this revelatory work is fascinating and thought-provoking, if, at the same time, oddly lacking in tension ...
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Its 114 minutes crackle with the nervous energy of revelation.
reviews.author: Spencer Ackerman

reviews.text: Adapting the cold language of data encryption to recount a dramatic saga of abuse of power and justified paranoia, Poitras brilliantly demonstrates that information is a weapon that cuts both ways.
reviews.author: Ronnie Scheib

reviews.text: Poitras delivers a mesmerizing look at both how Snowden managed to release his information as well as why it all matters.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

synopsis: After Laura Poitras received encrypted emails from someone with information on the government's massive covert-surveillance programs, she and reporter Glenn Greenwald flew to Hong Kong to meet the sender, who turned out to be Edward Snowden.
